claims.claim: No numpy.broadcast_to helper is registered, so np.broadcast_to(dist, shape, subok=False) falls back to ndarray and loses the Distribution wrapper instead of only decaying the samples.
claims.accuracy_evidence: The base function_helpers.py diff adds only is_distribution, get_n_samples, empty_like, broadcast_arrays and concatenate. It adds no broadcast_to entry, so core.py __array_function__ sends it to super().__array_function__.
claims.addressed_evidence: X adds a broadcast_to @function_helper that broadcasts array.distribution plus the sample axis; the result is rewrapped as a Distribution. Y adds a broadcast_to @dispatched_function that views samples as ndarray when subok=False and returns Distribution(new_samples).

claims.claim: The error message in ArrayDistribution.view has a second string without the f prefix, so {self.strides[-1]} and {self.dtype.itemsize} are never filled in.
claims.accuracy_evidence: In the base core.py ArrayDistribution.view, the final else raises ValueError(f"{self.__class__} can only be viewed with a dtype with " "itemsize {self.strides[-1]} or {self.dtype.itemsize}"). The second string is not an f-string.
claims.addressed_evidence: X rewrote the view ValueError messages without placeholder braces in plain strings. Y's messages put the f prefix on every string that has a placeholder, e.g. f"with itemsize {cur_dtype.itemsize} (i.e., ".
